description: The bar chart illustrates the average probing accuracy differences—expressed as percentage point differences—between two multilingual BERT models, mBERT and XLM-R, when probed using four different MLP (multilayer perceptron) configurations, as reported in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis lists the MLP variations by their hidden layer architecture and activation function: “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU.” The vertical axis, labeled “% point difference,” ranges from –0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at 0.1 intervals, indicating how much the probing accuracy of one model deviates from the other. Light blue bars represent mBERT, and dark blue bars represent XLM-R. For “hidden:[50], linear,” mBERT shows a negative difference (≈ –0.12), while XLM-R is slightly positive (≈ +0.02). For “hidden:[], linear,” both models show positive differences, with XLM-R (≈ +0.21) substantially outperforming mBERT (≈ +0.09). For “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is negative (≈ –0.11), while XLM-R is slightly positive (≈ +0.03). For “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” both models are negative, with mBERT at ≈ –0.18 and XLM-R at ≈ –0.13. The chart visually suggests that XLM-R generally performs better than mBERT across most configurations, particularly in the linear case with no hidden layers, while both models underperform with deeper ReLU networks.
